observation_summary: The method DiscreteDistribution.sample(int) throws an ArrayStoreException when the runtime class of the first element in the distribution does not match the type of subsequent elements returned by the sample() method.
hypothesis: The original implementation attempted to create a type-specific array using the class of the first element (singletons.get(0).getClass()). This is fundamentally flawed because the distribution may contain heterogeneous types that are subtypes of T, causing an ArrayStoreException when an element of a different subtype is inserted into the array.
prediction: Changing the array allocation from a type-specific array (using reflection) to a generic Object[] array will resolve the ArrayStoreException, as Object[] can store any object type.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the return type was changed from T[] to Object[] and the array allocation was changed from java.lang.reflect.Array.newInstance(...) to new Object[sampleSize]. This confirms that the procedural logic for array creation was the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic flaw in how the result array is initialized. The original code made an incorrect assumption that all elements in the distribution would share the same runtime class as the first element. This is a procedural error in the implementation of the sampling method, not a missing check or a simple value assignment. Therefore, it is classified as Algorithm/Method.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the return type changed from T[] to Object[]
The fix_diff_oracle shows the array allocation changed from reflection-based instantiation to new Object[sampleSize]
The bug report description explains that ArrayStoreException occurs when the first element's class differs from subsequent elements

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the return type changed, the root cause is the internal implementation of the array creation logic, not a mismatch in the contract between two components.
